wrapFetchWithPayment body-retry behavior.mechanism: new Request(input,init); clonedRequest=request.clone(); unpaid fetch(request); on 402, set PAYMENT-SIGNATURE on clonedRequest then fetch(clonedRequest.clone()) — Request.clone() preserves body stream bytes

notes.inspect: wrapFetchWithPayment has no inspect-only / dry-run mode; it auto-creates and sends payment on 402. Unpaid inspect requires calling plain fetch outside the wrapper.
notes.approve-gate: No first-class --approve. Closest native: x402Client.onBeforePaymentCreation abort hook or PaymentPolicy filter — still not an inspect-then-explicit-approve purchase flow.
notes.amountCap: x402Client SpendControls.maxAmountPerPayment (DEFAULT_MAX_AMOUNT_PER_PAYMENT="$1") enforced before policies; setSpendControls / config.spendControls. Not customer-x402 amountCapAtomic authorization binding.
notes.bodyBind: Transport-level: Request.clone() keeps exact POST body bytes on paid retry (proven). No auth-layer body-hash binding like customer-x402 authorization.
notes.reconcile: processPaymentResult recovered retry exists; no attempt-receipt schema, no reconcile CLI, no used/unused/expired confirmation vs finality.

unsupported: default unpaid inspect path inside wrapFetchWithPayment
explicit approve gate before signing/sending payment (customer-x402 --approve)
authorization object with amountCapAtomic + exact body/url/method binding
reconcile against RPC for used vs unused/expired/canceled with confirmation≠finality
purchase --attempt-receipt CLI / fundless inspection receipt workflow
conclusion: Current official @x402/fetch@2.25.0 + @x402/evm@2.25.0 CAN transport-consume POST /lockfile-pin-delta with exact body bytes on the paid retry (body reuse via Request.clone). They do NOT natively provide customer-x402's inspect / --approve / amountCapAtomic auth / attempt-receipt / reconcile stack — those remain gaps requiring the SDS customer-x402 wrapper or equivalent app policy.
